title: Searing Gorge
body: The Searing Gorge was born in fire. During the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan of the Dark Iron clan called upon powers sleeping beneath the world and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. Blackrock Mountain erupted, the Dark Iron capital was thrown down in ruin and the land around it was scorched black, leaving the Burning Steppes to the south and this ravaged valley to the north. Today the gorge is a place of ash, lava and ruthless industry. From Shadowforge City beneath the mountain the Dark Iron dwarves came looking for ore, dug the vast excavation called the Cauldron and filled it with slaves, golems and taskmasters. Fire elementals and lava spiders roam its slopes, and the Twilight's Hammer keeps a camp in the northwestern hills. Watching all of it from the cliffs of Thorium Point are the Thorium Brotherhood, Dark Iron smiths who broke with their own kin. To the northeast, the locked gates of Stonewrought Pass shut the gorge away from Loch Modan.

title: Thorium Point
body: Thorium Point clings to the cliffs in the north of the gorge, a guarded outpost looking straight down into the Cauldron. It is the stronghold of the Thorium Brotherhood, Dark Iron smiths who left their clan and now keep a close eye on everything their former kin do below. Brotherhood lookouts stand watch over the camp, and a wanted board posts bounties against the Dark Iron crews and the thieves who rob the camp. Gryphon and wind rider handlers both keep their mounts here, for the Brotherhood welcomes Alliance and Horde alike, and travelers of either banner come to trade with the master craftsmen of the Point.

title: The Cauldron
body: At the heart of the gorge lies the Cauldron, an enormous pit the Dark Iron dwarves carved out of the blackened valley floor in their hunger for ore. Scaffolds and cart lines cling to its walls, and heavy war golems lumber along its ramps. Slave workers toil without rest under the whips of Dark Iron slavers and taskmasters, so broken by the labor and the heat that they turn on anyone who interferes, would-be rescuers included. Four sentry towers guard the rim, and fire and magma elementals drift through the crevices below. Even here there is trade: the cutthroat dealers of the Undermarket have set up shop in the Cauldron under the protection of their Dark Iron partners.

title: The Slag Pit
body: The Slag Pit is the mine beneath the Cauldron, a maze of hot tunnels rich in ore. Its Dark Iron crew answers to Overseer Maltorius, once of the Thorium Brotherhood, and sleeps in quarters deep inside. Pools of lava in the lower tunnels are home to ravenous incendosaurs. In one hidden chamber stands the altar of Suntara, where enslaved archaeologists labor without rest around a silent, hulking form called Obsidion. The Dark Irons guard the pit fiercely against anyone who would meddle with their work.

parts.body: The captives are the excavation team of Dorius Stonetender, taken from the Grimesilt Dig Site. The power of the Suntara stones has bent their minds to the building of Obsidion, and it drives them on even after their bodies give out. One of them, dying, gasps that the altar of Suntara is the key to their release.

title: Firewatch Ridge
body: The mountains of the northwestern gorge belong to the Twilight's Hammer. Their encampment on Firewatch Ridge is held by fire guards, geomancers and dark shamans, while idolaters carry the cult's relics and symbols of Ragnaros, and Highlord Mastrogonde walks among them. The cult keeps a grim warning on the ridge: a cage holding the spirit of a night elf who once served it, put to death as a blasphemer when he turned back to Elune. Greater lava spiders hunt the slopes around the camp, and lava crabs and fire beetles crawl among the rocks.

title: Grimesilt Dig Site
body: The Grimesilt Dig Site was once worked by the dwarves of Ironforge, but the Dark Iron dwarves have since taken it, and their geologists now work the ground under the watch of watchmen and tempered war golems. Of the last Ironforge excavation to dig here, only its leader, Dorius Stonetender, remains, stretched out on the ground among the diggings, and of his team there is no sign. Another dwarf's luck is merely embarrassing. When a crew member named Locheed hid from the geologists in an outhouse, they simply locked the door behind him and kept the key, and from inside he still begs passersby for help, and for some silk cloth.

parts.body: This is where Dorius's fall began. Unmasked as Lathoric the Black, he would boast that it was at this dig site that he came upon the Suntara stones and felt the power of Ragnaros flood into him. The find that seemed to doom his excavation team was, for him, a rebirth.

title: Dustfire Valley
body: Dustfire Valley is a windswept cut through the northeastern gorge, running north toward Stonewrought Pass and the road to Loch Modan beyond. The Dark Irons hold it as they hold most of the gorge: their geologists search the valley for ore, guarded by tempered war golems, while glassweb spiders spin among the rocks. With the gates of the pass kept locked, the valley leads nowhere for most travelers.

title: Stonewrought Pass
body: Stonewrought Pass is a dwarven tunnel joining the Searing Gorge to Loch Modan, the work of Franclorn Forgewright, the architect whose stonewrought method of building also raised the great dam of Loch Modan. For years both ends have been sealed with locked gates. On the Loch Modan side a mountaineer keeps the key and turns nearly every traveler away, so most who reach the gorge come by the long road through the Badlands or down from Blackrock Mountain instead.

title: Tanner Camp
body: In the southeast of the gorge stands Tanner Camp, the lonely tent of Sarah Tanner, a master of elemental leatherworking who teaches the craft to those willing to open their minds to the greater powers of substance. Her choice of home is a dangerous one: glassweb spiders hunt the surrounding rocks, the great spider Rekk'tilac roams nearby, and a long passage behind her tent leads toward the lair of Margol the Rager.

title: The Sea of Cinders
body: South of the Cauldron the gorge opens into the Sea of Cinders, a broad flat waste scorched by fire and scoured by hot wind. Ash and embers still rise from the smoldering ground and hang in the air, and little lives here that is not made of flame or used to it: searing lava spiders, magma elementals and fire beetles. Dark Iron lookouts keep watch over the plain, which stretches to the foot of Blackrock Mountain.

title: Blackchar Cave
body: In the southwestern corner of the gorge, close under Blackrock Mountain, lies Blackchar Cave, a mysterious cavern that has been sealed shut. What lies within is unknown. The ground before it is anything but quiet: Anvilrage guards from the Dark Iron city patrol nearby, lava spiders and fire beetles creep among the rocks, and the fire lord Overmaster Pyron burns at the approach to the Blackrock quarry.

title: Blackrock Mountain
body: The southwestern road of the gorge climbs to Blackrock Mountain, the volcano that rose when Thaurissan's summoning brought Ragnaros into the world. Within it lie Shadowforge City, capital of the Dark Iron dwarves, and above it the fortress of Blackrock Spire, raised by Dark Iron hands under the Firelord's will and now held by the orcs of the Blackrock clan. On the gorge side, quarry slaves cut stone under the eyes of Anvilrage guards, and a hulking foe known as the Behemoth roams the approach.

title: Kalaran Windblade
body: Kalaran Windblade keeps a lonely camp on the slopes between Thorium Point and the Cauldron, with no company but his lumbering squire, Maltrake, who says he lives only to serve his master. Kalaran tells of a father slain by the filth of the Cauldron and of Stormwind magistrates who would not even admit this corner of the world exists, and he swears that riches beyond imagining await anyone who helps him take his revenge. When he works his craft he chants in a tongue no one recognizes, and the effort drops him to one knee.

parts.body: His grief was a mask. When the towers of the Cauldron burned, the wronged man was gone and a drake of the black dragonflight stood in his place, a servant of the legion of Blackrock. The murdered father was only bait: no mortal, the drake mocked, would have lent a hand had Blackrock simply asked.

title: Overseer Oilfist
body: Overseer Oilfist leads the Thorium Brotherhood from Thorium Point. Under his hand the Brotherhood smiths and trades in the shadow of the Dark Iron works below, a company of dwarves who chose to leave the protection and comfort of the Depths to explore the world, or to exploit it, as one of them lets slip. His people are an odd lot, from a blind and tipsy lookout captain to an enforcer laid low by swollen fingers. Oilfist himself does not forgive desertion. When Maltorius left the Brotherhood to command the Dark Iron crew of the Slag Pit, it was by Oilfist's own order that a bounty was posted for the traitor's head.

title: Master Smith Burninate
body: Master Smith Burninate is the forge master of Thorium Point, a gruff dwarf who sells a little food and drink on the side. His great worry is fiery flux, the Brotherhood's prized smithing reagent. When Maltorius deserted, he took the secret recipe with him, something more valuable than a pristine arcane crystal, and Burninate would bet anything it paid for the traitor's new promotion among the Dark Irons. He wants the plans back, and is sure they lie somewhere near Maltorius, deep inside the Slag Pit.
sources: npc_text 7115, 7121 (Burninate gossip)
quest 7722 description and reward text
quests 7736, 8241, 8242 completion texts (dwindling fiery flux supply)
notes: Converted: the recovery of the plans and what follows (7722 reward text, the flux supply quests offered afterwards, the Lokhtos referral) moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 7722). The opening adds the 7722 description (more valuable than a pristine arcane crystal, part of the deal in his promotion). Dialogue reread: npc_text 7115, 7121 are classic text. Earlier: verified. parts.body: With the plans recovered, Burninate hoped the traitor's teeth had been kicked in too, and got down to business: rebuilding the Brotherhood's dwindling supply of fiery flux from incendosaur scales, coal and whatever else its friends will bring. Those who prove themselves trusted friends of the Brotherhood he sends on to Lokhtos Darkbargainer at the Grim Guzzler in Blackrock Depths.

title: Lookout Captain Lolo Longstriker
body: The captain of the Thorium Point lookouts is, by his own cheerful admission, as blind as a bat and seldom sober. Lolo Longstriker insists that drink keeps his remaining senses sharp, since everyone knows a dwarf who loses one sense gains in the others, and claims his sense for drink has never been better. It is he who pays the bounty on Overseer Maltorius, posted by Oilfist's order, though those who come to collect may find him too busy hiccuping to notice them.

parts.body: When the traitor's severed head was finally set before him, Lolo greeted it with slurred delight. He never thought he would see that ugly mug again, he declared, and the old face looked better without the rest of him attached.

title: Hansel Heavyhands
body: Hansel Heavyhands is the Brotherhood's enforcer, the dwarf they call in when Lolo would rather not spill his ale. He would gladly deal out the pain himself, he says, were it not for his swollen fingers, his bunions and a cold he blames on the frigid climate of the Searing Gorge. Instead he hands the work to others: smashing the heavy war golems around the Cauldron, culling the greater lava spiders, and clearing the incendosaurs from the lava pools of the Slag Pit so the Brotherhood can explore below.
sources: npc_text 7117 (Hansel gossip)

title: Overseer Maltorius
body: Maltorius was once an agent of the Thorium Brotherhood. He went over to the Dark Irons and was rewarded with command of the Slag Pit crew in the Cauldron, a promotion the Brotherhood suspects he bought with their secret recipe for fiery flux. He now rules the mine from deep within its tunnels. At Thorium Point his name is spoken with contempt, and a bounty on his head hangs on the camp's wanted board.

title: Dorius Stonetender
body: Dorius Stonetender, brother of Curator Thorius of the Hall of Explorers, led an Ironforge excavation at the Grimesilt Dig Site. Now he lies sprawled among the diggings, groaning that he is bleeding inside and must get back to Ironforge. He makes a trying companion on the road, forever stopping to catch his breath and swearing he must quit smoking, yet quick with his fists when the Dark Irons close in. His one worry, he says, is his team: if anything ever happened to him, they would be stuck in the Cauldron's mine forever.

parts.body: He never reached safety. Short of the gate a Dark Iron marksman brought him down, and the dwarf was gone in a cloud of dust, leaving only a singed letter for his brother. Written as a dead man's last words, it told that the Dark Irons held the Suntara stones and that their leader, Lathoric the Black, was using them to enslave the excavation team.
sources: smart_scripts 8284 and action list 828405 (Dark Iron Marksman summoned, Man Down, letter object 175704 summoned, quest explored)
creature_text 8284 groups 5, 7 (He got me; disappears in a cloud of dust)
quest 3367 reward text (letter dropped by Dorius when he was shot)
quest 3368 description (the letter)

parts.body: Dorius never died. At the Grimesilt Dig Site he had stumbled upon the Suntara stones, and the power of Ragnaros surged through him. The Firelord gave him a purpose and a new name, Lathoric the Black, acolyte of fire. His wound and his death were a ruse to play on his brother's grief and draw in rescuers. He means his creation Obsidion to destroy the Blackrock orcs of the Spire and unite the Dark Irons with their brethren in the fiery depths below.
sources: creature_text 8421 groups 0-4, 6 (Lathoric's confession)
smart_scripts 8417 (Lathoric 8391 spawned on accepting 3566), 8391 and 839101
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lathoric_the_Black (Lathoric is Dorius)

title: Zamael Lunthistle
body: In a cage on Firewatch Ridge lingers the spirit of Zamael Lunthistle. As a young night elf in Darkshore he fell in with the Twilight's Hammer and abandoned his faith in Elune, until a vision from the goddess woke him. In repentance he began a prayer etched on a tablet of pure gold, but the cult found it, branded him a blasphemer and put him to death. Bound to the world and caged as a warning to traitors, he asks only that his unfinished prayer be carried to the Temple of the Moon.
sources: npc_text 1920-1922 (Zamael's tale)
quests 3377, 3378 (descriptions and reward texts)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide and nothing from a later era. His tale and death are what he tells on meeting (gossip 1285-1287, npc_text 1920-1922, classic text); the prayer's delivery (3378) is not told. Earlier: verified. Faction 0 confirmed: faction template 534 (Alliance Generic, no reputation, no enemy group) leaves him neutral to the Horde, so his gossip tale can be heard by both; his quests are Alliance only. Check: his tale (npc_text 1921, 1922) sits behind the gossip option of menu 1285, which conditions show only while quest 3377 (Hear Zamael tell his tale) is in the log, so Alliance hear it at the first meeting; it is backstory he tells himself, not an outcome, and Firewatch Ridge tells the same to everyone. Horde can still talk to him (template 534, neutral), so faction 0 stands.

title: Margol the Rager
body: Margol the Rager is a monstrous beast that haunts the southeasternmost corner of the gorge, at the end of a long passage behind Sarah Tanner's camp. Mountaineer Pebblebitty, keeper of the gate at Stonewrought Pass, has faced her and calls her a lady almost as tough as herself, and she names Margol as the test for anyone who wants a key to the pass. Lodged in the beast's gigantic horn, among its scratches and cracks, is the proof of that old meeting: the broken head of an axe etched with Pebblebitty's name.
sources: quest 3181 description (scratches and cracks, axe head of Mountaineer Pebblebitty lodged in the horn)
npc_text 1838 (southeasternmost corner, a lady almost as tough as me, proof of heroics for a key)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tanner_Camp (passage behind her tent to Margol)
quest 3182 reward text, quest 3201 description
notes: Converted: Thorius's verdict on the horn (3182 reward text) and his remark on the 'incident' (3201 description, offered at that turn-in) moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 3182; Alliance only part on a faction 0 entry). The opening keeps Pebblebitty's own words (npc_text 1838) and the axe head seen on the horn (3181 description, read on looting the horn after the kill, the entry trigger); passage behind Tanner Camp from the wiki, as in 5108. Pebblebitty's npc_text 1833-1839 reread: classic text. Earlier: verified. Check: part 1 reworded so it does not repeat The Key to the Gorge part 2 (same trigger, DONE 3182); the 'incident' stays here, the museum and the proof of deed there. No Horde route: the horn chain 3181, 3182, 3201 is Alliance only and no other quest involves Margol, so this stays an Alliance only part on a faction 0 entry.

parts.body: Curator Thorius of Ironforge knew Margol's horn for what it was and hailed the beast as the bane of every archaeologist who ever dug in the Searing Gorge. Of Pebblebitty's old meeting with Margol he would say only that there had been 'the incident', and that the mountaineer had long wanted to kill the beast herself.
sources: quest 3182 reward text (bane of every archaeologist)
quest 3201 description (jealous, the 'incident'), offered by Thorius 8256 on the turn-in of 3182

title: Overmaster Pyron
body: Overmaster Pyron is a lord of fire who guards the quarry at the foot of Blackrock Mountain, a foul spirit the Dark Iron dwarves summoned into the world. The mages Jalinda Sprig sent from Morgan's Vigil came back burned or worse, and the elders heeded by Thunderheart of Kargath felt his presence as a disturbance among the elements, a disharmony of flame that threatens the land with endless drought. Both want him ended: the elders to heal the disharmony, Jalinda so that her expedition can make its way into Blackrock Depths.
sources: quest 3906 description (Dark Irons summoned a foul spirit, eternal drought, lord of fire at the quarry)
quest 4262 description (mages came back crispy or worse; expedition crew to get into Blackrock Depths; Pyron guards the entrance at the Blackrock Quarry)
creature_text 9026
quests 3907, 4263
notes: Converted: his death cry naming Incendius (creature_text 9026, said on death) moved from the opening to part 1 (KILL 9026, also an entry trigger). Incendius's own master is left unnamed: that is the Blackrock Depths revelation (3907, 4263), not this zone's. The opening adds why Jalinda and Thunderheart want him gone (3906 eternal drought, 4262 the way into the Depths). Entry triggers ACCEPT 3906 and 4262 kept as they were: both are filed under Blackrock Mountain (QuestSortID 25) and their givers stand in Kargath and Morgan's Vigil. Earlier: verified. Check: ACCEPT 3906 and 4262 are used by no other file (badlands.json and burning_steppes.json do not name Pyron).

parts.body: Pyron does not fall quietly. As he dies he swears that he will be reborn, for Lord Incendius shall raise him from the ashes, a sign that the fire lord of the quarry is only the servant of a greater power deeper within the mountain.
sources: creature_text 9026 (I will be reborn, Incendius shall raise me), smart_scripts 9026 (said on death)
quest 3906 reward text (Pyron's destruction merely lifted a veil, a more insidious source within Blackrock)
quest 4263 description (Incendius continues to raise Pyron)

title: Divine Retribution
body: Kalaran Windblade asks for help avenging his father, slain by the filth of the Cauldron, since the magistrates of Stormwind will do nothing. His plan is bold: set the four sentry towers ablaze and blind the Dark Iron defenses before an offensive. For that he needs a torch of flawless flame, made from the hearts of fire elementals and golem oil, a shaft reforged from the thorium daggers of Cauldron taskmasters and slavers, and a casing drawn from a Twilight's Hammer symbol of Ragnaros. Once the torch is made, his squire Maltrake will explain how it is to be used.
sources: npc_text 1954 (father slain, Stormwind magistrate)
quests 3441, 3442, 3443, 3452, 3462 descriptions
quest 3463 reward text
creature_text 8480, 8509 (the reveal)
gameobject 149502 Hoard of the Black Dragonflight
quest 4022 (molt shown to Cyrus Therepentous, Burning Steppes)
smart_scripts 8509, 8479
notes: Converted: the burning towers, the reveal, the trinkets and the molt moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 3463, the turn-in to Squire Maltrake that starts the scene). The opening is the plan and the three parts of the torch (3442, 3443, 3452) up to Maltrake (3462). Cyrus and the molt's use are left to burning_steppes.json 4618 (ACCEPT 4022 is its trigger). Dialogue reread: npc_text 1953-1955 and creature_text 8479, 8480, 8509 are classic text.

parts.body: When the four towers burn, Squire Maltrake calls the sight glorious, and his master agrees, for it all went exactly as he planned. Kalaran casts off his disguise. He is a black drake, and the fires were set to open the gorge to the legion of Blackrock. Mockingly he lets his helpers live to see the chaos to come, leaves them a chest of trinkets and a molt of his flight that his kin in the Burning Steppes will know how to use, and takes wing.
sources: quest 3463 reward text (It is glorious!)
creature_text 8480, 8509 (the reveal)
smart_scripts 8509, 8479 (Kalaran the Deceiver 8480 summoned on turning in 3463)
gameobject 149502 Hoard of the Black Dragonflight (quest 3481)

title: The Suntara Stones
body: At the Grimesilt Dig Site lies Dorius Stonetender, leader of an Ironforge excavation, groaning that he is badly hurt, bleeding inside, and must get back to Ironforge. Help him up and he sets off for the gate at Stonewrought Pass, though he must stop again and again to catch his breath. On the way he points out the Cauldron and begs that it be remembered: if anything ever happened to him, he says, his team would be stuck in that mine forever. The Dark Irons do not mean to let him go easily.
sources: quests 3367, 3368, 3371, 3372, 3566 (descriptions and reward texts)
creature_text 8284, 8391, 8421
smart_scripts 8284, 8417, 8391
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lathoric_the_Black
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 3367 (Dorius found and helped toward the gate, creature_text 8284 on the escort). Parts follow the chain: 1 the ambush and the letter (QUEST_DONE 3367, ACCEPT 3368), 2 Thorius's vow and the dying archaeologist's plea (QUEST_DONE 3371; Thorius's vow at DONE 3368 always precedes it), 3 the trap and the Lathoric reveal (ACCEPT 3566, which summons Lathoric and Dorius), 4 Thorius's reaction (QUEST_DONE 3566). 'the gate at Stonewrought Pass' from the escort ending at the gate (creature_text 8284 group 4), its waypoint path 82840 ending at -6388,-1983 in Dustfire Valley beside the pass door 150137. Obsidion's purpose stays in the Dorius entry. Alliance only (AllowableRaces 1101). Check: old part 2 split so each piece is told where it happens: Thorius's vow and the order to search the Slag Pit to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 3368, whose reward text is the vow and which offers 3371), the dying archaeologist's plea to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 3371); old parts 3 and 4 renumbered 4 and 5.

parts.body: Within sight of the gate a Dark Iron marksman shoots him down, and Dorius vanishes in a cloud of dust, leaving a singed letter for his brother, Curator Thorius. It says the Suntara stones are real and in Dark Iron hands, that their leader Lathoric the Black uses them to enslave the excavation team, and that the captives toil in the Cauldron on something called Obsidion. Help them, it begs: it is the final wish of a dead man.
sources: smart_scripts 828404, 828405 (Dark Iron Marksman summoned, Dorius falls, letter 175704 summoned)
creature_text 8284 groups 5-7
quest 3367 reward text
quest 3368 description (the letter)

parts.body: Thorius sobbed over the letter, then wiped his face dry and vowed in the name of the Light that his brother would have his wish. With an empty hole where his heart had been, he sent rescuers back to the gorge to free Dorius's men from the sweltering mine the Dark Irons call the Slag Pit, and to see the murderers brought to justice.
sources: quest 3368 completion and reward texts (Thorius sobs, wipes his face, vows in the name of the Light)
quest 3371 description (empty hole where my heart used to be; free his men; Slag Pit; perpetrators brought to justice), offered by Thorius 8256 on the turn-in of 3368 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: Deep in the pit, one of the enslaved archaeologists lies dying. Forget me, he pleads, help the others. The power of the Suntara will not let them rest even once their bodies fail, and only the altar of Suntara can release them: a relic held by the Twilight's Hammer in the hills to the northwest must be laid upon it.
sources: quest 3371 reward text (forget about me, help the others)
quest 3372 description, offered by the Dying Archaeologist 8417 on the turn-in of 3371

parts.body: It was a trap. The relic was the last Suntara stone Lathoric needed, and the dying archaeologist can only beg forgiveness as Dorius himself appears, alive and mocking. Playing on his brother's grief, he says, was all it took to bring rescuers to fetch it. Then Lathoric the Black, as Dorius is now named, calls Obsidion to rise and serve its master.
sources: quest 3566 description (it was all a trap)
creature_text 8421 (Bravo! You thought I was dead?; played upon my brother; last Suntara stone)
creature_text 8391 (Obsidion, rise and serve your master)
smart_scripts 8417 (Lathoric spawned on accepting 3566)

parts.body: When the head of Lathoric and the heart of Obsidion are laid before Thorius, the curator turns white. His own brother had set it all up, betraying him and all of Ironforge. Grief gives way to fury, and then to fear: if so noble a dwarf could be turned so easily to the will of Ragnaros, the influence of the Old Gods is still strong in these lands, and no one is safe.
sources: quest 3566 log description and reward text

title: The Key to the Gorge
body: Mountaineer Pebblebitty will not open the gate at Stonewrought Pass. The gorge is full of beasts that have killed good dwarves, she says, and if she lets one traveler in she will have to let in everyone. Pressed, she admits there is a back road the orcs paved through the Badlands near Kargath, and offers a key to anyone who returns with proof of heroics, pointing to Margol the Rager in the far southeast of the gorge. Margol's gigantic horn once carried Pebblebitty's own broken axe head, but it shatters into a million pieces when pulled free.
sources: npc_text 1833-1839 (Pebblebitty)
quests 3181, 3182, 3201 (descriptions and reward texts)
notes: Converted: the opening is the premise up to quest 3181 (the entry trigger, offered by the horn itself, whose text has the axe head shattering). Parts: 1 Pebblebitty calls it a fake and sends it to Thorius (QUEST_DONE 3181), 2 Thorius validates it and signs the proof of deed (QUEST_DONE 3182), 3 the key is handed over (QUEST_DONE 3201). 3182 and 3201 are filed under Loch Modan and Ironforge but used by no other file. Back road paved by the orcs from npc_text 1835. Pebblebitty's npc_text reread: classic text. Alliance only (AllowableRaces 1101). Removed in Cataclysm, present in 3.3.5. Check: part 2 reworded so it does not repeat the Margol part 1 wording (same trigger, DONE 3182).

parts.body: Without the axe head, Pebblebitty calls the horn an obvious fake. She has been face to face with Margol, she insists, and the real horn is eight times larger; this one surely came off some stormsnout in the Barrens. If Curator Thorius in Ironforge will vouch for it, she says, a proof of deed will earn the key.
sources: quest 3181 reward text
quest 3182 description

parts.body: In Ironforge, Curator Thorius could hardly believe his eyes: this was the horn of Margol the Rager, scourge of every archaeologist who ever worked the gorge, and might he keep it for the museum? After such a contribution a proof of deed was no trouble. As he filled out the large document, he confided that Pebblebitty was only jealous.
sources: quest 3182 reward text
quest 3201 description (offered by Thorius on the turn-in of 3182)

parts.body: Pebblebitty could not argue with the curator's signature. A deal is a deal, she grumbled, though she could not see how someone so weak had overcome Margol, and she handed over the key to the Searing Gorge with a warning: whatever happens beyond the gate is the bearer's own fault.
sources: quest 3201 reward text

title: The Brotherhood and the Slag Pit
body: The Thorium Brotherhood has a quarrel with the Slag Pit, and it is personal. Overseer Maltorius, one of their own, deserted to take command of the Dark Iron crew there, and the Brotherhood believes he paid for the post with their recipe for fiery flux. Thorium Point answers with every weapon it has. Master Smith Burninate wants the stolen plans back, the wanted board offers a bounty on Maltorius's head, and Taskmaster Scrange pays to cull the Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers and to recover a spyglass and smithing tuyere stolen from the camp. Evonice Sootsmoker has a subtler idea: steal the crew's pillows, for a Dark Iron cannot sleep without one. Hansel Heavyhands wants golems, lava spiders and incendosaurs cleared so Brotherhood teams can explore the pit.
sources: quests 7701, 7702, 7722, 7723, 7724, 7727, 7728, 7729 (descriptions and reward texts)
notes: Converted: the recovered plans and the flux supply moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 7722). The pillow raid's result (sleepless Dark Irons going home to the Depths, 7702 reward text) moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 7702); the opening now gives only Evonice's reasoning (7702 description). The two parts are independent turn-ins, so each reads on from the opening alone. Maltorius's death is told in the Lolo Longstriker entry. Dialogue reread: Brotherhood npc_text 7094, 7095, 7115, 7117, 7120, 7121 are classic; Oilfist's 17268 (Cataclysm) unused. Check: part 1 reworded so it does not repeat the Burninate part 1 wording (same trigger, DONE 7722).

parts.body: With the stolen plans back at Thorium Point, the recipe for fiery flux belongs to the Brotherhood again, and the quarrel can give way to the forge. Stocks of flux are running low, so Burninate now takes incendosaur scales, coal and other goods from the Brotherhood's friends to make more.
sources: quest 7722 reward text
quests 7736, 8241, 8242 completion texts

parts.body: Evonice's scheme worked, or so she says. With their pillows gone, the sleepy Dark Irons of the Slag Pit began heading back to their homes in the Depths for rest, and the work of the pit slowed. Crazy goggles or not, she reminds anyone who doubts her, she is the smart one.
sources: quest 7702 reward text and completion text (the crazy goggles, I'm the smart one)

title: The Undermarket
body: Nilith Lokrav is a tailor who prizes the shadow silk spun by the spiders of the gorge, a cloth highly sought after by the artisans of her trade. She works in the south of the gorge with Raze, the hulking guardian who smashes on command. Lately a band of shadowsilk poachers has encroached on these lands, slaying spiders by the score without a thought for the future, and Nilith wants them found and ended, beginning in the north. Raze is eager to help: use the staff of command near a poacher, and he will make them rue the day they came to poach here.
sources: quests 3379, 3385, 3402 (descriptions and reward texts)
creature_text 8439, 8441 (Raze and the staff)
DB spawns: Nilith Lokrav 8439 and Raze 8441 in the south of the gorge, Kovic 8444 and Clunk 8447 in area 246
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 3379 (the poachers). The Undermarket and the order to kill Kovic moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 3385, offered when 3379 is turned in); Kovic's death to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 3385); Vizzklick's reaction to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 3402, turned in to Vizzklick 6568 in Gadgetzan; filed under Tailoring, used by no other file). The Undermarket's base in the Cauldron stays in the Cauldron entry as something anyone sees there. Earlier: verified. Tailoring profession chain (skill 197), open to both factions.

parts.body: The poachers were only the beginning. Nilith names a greater enemy: the Undermarket, cutthroat traders who will sell, move or do just about anything for the right price. They have set up a base in the Cauldron under Trade Master Kovic, who keeps close ties with the Dark Iron dwarves, and Nilith wants Kovic and his minion Clunk slain to send a message to their leadership.
sources: quest 3385 description (offered by Nilith on the turn-in of 3379)

parts.body: Kovic and Clunk fell in the Cauldron, a decisive blow that Nilith expects will make the Undermarket's leaders think twice before sending more cronies into the gorge. The trader's satchel held nothing of use to her, but the news itself she sends on to Vizzklick in Gadgetzan, sure he will be glad to hear it.
sources: quest 3385 reward text
quest 3402 description (offered on the turn-in of 3385)

parts.body: Vizzklick could hardly believe it, and called it a glorious day. For years, he says, Kovic ran shady trades for the Undermarket, undercutting honest, hard working traders all over the world, and whoever ended him has earned a fine reward.
sources: quest 3402 reward text
